title: Seventh Word The Universes Talisman Soldier Comparison With Talisman Medicine And Ticket

questions.question: What central statement of faith is introduced at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the Last Day.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the two parts of that statement help solve?
questions.answer: They help explain the mystery of creation and open the way to true happiness for the human soul.

questions.question: Which religious acts are described as supplies for the life to come and light for the grave?
questions.answer: Listening to the Qur’an, following its commands, performing the required prayers, and avoiding major sins.

questions.question: What kind of teaching method does the passage use after the opening lines?
questions.answer: It uses a comparison or parable.

questions.question: In what setting does the soldier face his crisis?
questions.answer: He is in a place of battle and testing.

questions.question: What dangers surround the soldier in the comparison?
questions.answer: He has two severe wounds, a lion behind him, a gallows in front of him, and a long journey ahead.

questions.question: How does the soldier first feel when he thinks about his condition?
questions.answer: He feels hopeless and full of fear.

questions.question: Who comes to help the soldier, and how is he described?
questions.answer: A bright, kind figure appears, shining like Khidr.

questions.question: What promise is made about the two talismans if the soldier uses them correctly?
questions.answer: The lion will become like a tame riding animal, and the gallows will become something enjoyable instead of terrifying.

questions.question: What change is promised for the soldier’s wounds through the two medicines?
questions.answer: They will change from painful wounds into sweet-smelling flowers.

questions.question: What benefit comes with the ticket given to the soldier?
questions.answer: It allows him to complete a very long journey with great ease and speed.

questions.question: How is the soldier encouraged to confirm that these gifts are real?
questions.answer: He is told to test them and see for himself.

questions.question: What happens when the soldier tries what he was given?
questions.answer: He finds that it is true.

questions.question: How does Said connect himself to the comparison at the end of the target passage?
questions.answer: He says he also tested it personally and found it completely true.

questions.question: What practices are presented as especially valuable for the journey to eternity?
questions.answer: Hearing the Qur’an, obeying it, praying regularly, and staying away from grave sins.

questions.question: Who is the main character in the comparison?
questions.answer: A soldier.

questions.question: What do the two wounds suggest about the seriousness of his condition?
questions.answer: They show that his suffering is deep and urgent.

questions.question: What does the lion contribute to the soldier’s fear?
questions.answer: It represents a threat that seems ready to attack at any moment.

questions.question: What does the gallows suggest about what may happen to both the soldier and those he loves?
questions.answer: It suggests destruction, loss, and the ending of life.

questions.question: What makes the journey ahead feel even harder for the soldier?
questions.answer: It is long, and he is being driven into exile.

questions.question: Why is the appearance of the shining helper important in the comparison?
questions.answer: It introduces mercy, guidance, and a way out of despair.

questions.question: What three kinds of help does the shining figure offer?
questions.answer: Two talismans, two medicines, and a ticket.

questions.question: What is the condition for the promised benefits to appear?
questions.answer: The soldier must use what he is given properly and follow the instructions.

questions.question: What does the soldier’s experiment show about faith-based guidance in the comparison?
questions.answer: It shows that the guidance works in reality, not only in theory.

questions.question: Why is the final statement by Said important?
questions.answer: It strengthens the comparison by adding personal confirmation that the lesson is true.

questions.question: What two beliefs are placed at the center of this passage?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah and faith in the Last Day.

questions.question: According to the opening sentence, what effect do these beliefs have on the human spirit?
questions.answer: They open the path to happiness and help resolve deep confusion.

questions.question: What does the passage compare reliance on Allah, patience, prayer, and gratitude to?
questions.answer: It compares them to useful and healing medicine.

questions.question: What does it compare Qur’anic listening, obedience, prayer, and avoiding major sins to?
questions.answer: It compares them to tickets, provisions, and light for the next life.

questions.question: What kind of person is used in the comparison to represent the human condition?
questions.answer: A soldier in severe danger.

questions.question: List the four major troubles facing the soldier.
questions.answer: Two serious wounds, a lion behind him, a gallows in front of him, and a long journey ahead.

questions.question: What emotional state is the soldier in before help arrives?
questions.answer: He is overwhelmed by fear and despair.

questions.question: What transformation is promised for the lion?
questions.answer: It will become a gentle mount instead of a deadly threat.

questions.question: What transformation is promised for the gallows?
questions.answer: It will become something like a swing that brings enjoyment rather than terror.

questions.question: How are the soldier’s wounds described after the medicines take effect?
questions.answer: They become beautiful and fragrant like flowers.

questions.question: What does the ticket make possible that seemed impossible before?
questions.answer: It makes a very long trip suddenly manageable and swift.

questions.question: Why is the command to test the claims important for comprehension of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that the truth being described is meant to be experienced and verified.

questions.question: What phrase in Arabic is the passage built around in meaning?
questions.answer: The declaration of belief in Allah and the Last Day.

questions.question: What two big human needs are those beliefs said to address?
questions.answer: Understanding existence and finding happiness for the soul.

questions.question: What spiritual actions are described as remedies in the opening lines?
questions.answer: Depending on Allah, turning to Him with patience and supplication, and thanking Him.

questions.question: What acts of worship are described as preparation for the hereafter?
questions.answer: Listening to the Qur’an, obeying it, performing the prayers, and leaving major sins.

questions.question: Why is the soldier a fitting example for the passage’s lesson?
questions.answer: He is in extreme danger and needs rescue, just as people face deep spiritual and life struggles.

questions.question: Which threats in the comparison come from behind and from in front of the soldier?
questions.answer: The lion is behind him, and the gallows is in front of him.

questions.question: What do the wounds add to the soldier’s overall condition?
questions.answer: They show that he is already suffering badly even before the other dangers reach him.

questions.question: What does the long journey suggest about the future facing the soldier?
questions.answer: It suggests a difficult path that cannot be avoided.

questions.question: How does the helper first deal with the soldier’s emotional state?
questions.answer: He tells him not to give up hope.

questions.question: What is special about the way the helper presents his gifts?
questions.answer: He explains both what they are and what changes they can bring.

questions.question: What is the relationship between proper use and promised benefit in the comparison?
questions.answer: The benefit depends on using the gifts correctly and as instructed.

questions.question: What does the soldier’s partial testing of the gifts lead him to conclude?
questions.answer: He concludes that the promises are true.

questions.question: How does the mention of “this unfortunate Said” shape the tone of the ending?
questions.answer: It makes the lesson personal and sincere, as if the speaker has lived the truth of it.

questions.question: What are the “two parts” of the faith statement mentioned at the start?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the Last Day.

questions.question: What does the passage say these two beliefs do for the puzzle of existence?
questions.answer: They act like keys that make its hidden meaning understandable.

questions.question: How are patience, prayer, trust, and gratitude described in relation to a believer’s struggles?
questions.answer: They are described as helpful cures and supports.

questions.question: What future-oriented benefits are connected to following the Qur’an and worshiping properly?
questions.answer: They prepare a person for eternity, provide for the hereafter, and bring light to the grave.

questions.question: What image is used to begin the main comparison of the passage?
questions.answer: A wounded soldier in a terrifying situation.

questions.question: What shows that the soldier is trapped between immediate danger and future fear?
questions.answer: He faces threats around him at the moment and also a hard journey ahead.

questions.question: In what way does the helper appear different from the surrounding scene?
questions.answer: He appears bright, kind, and full of hope in the middle of fear and darkness.

questions.question: What three gifts does the helper offer, and what need does each one address?
questions.answer: Talismans for danger, medicines for wounds, and a ticket for the journey.

questions.question: What do the promised changes in the lion and gallows teach about the power of true guidance?
questions.answer: They teach that what seems terrifying can become bearable or even beneficial through right belief.

questions.question: What does the transformation of the wounds into flowers suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that pain can be changed into something meaningful and beautiful.

questions.question: Why does the helper invite the soldier to experiment instead of only demanding belief?
questions.answer: He wants the soldier to recognize the truth through experience.

questions.question: What is the result of the soldier’s trial of the helper’s words?
questions.answer: He confirms that they are true.

questions.question: How does the speaker’s own testimony affect the reliability of the comparison?
questions.answer: It gives added weight because he says he personally tested the matter and found it true.

questions.question: According to the passage, what two beliefs are like powerful keys for human life?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah and faith in the Last Day.

questions.question: What two major outcomes do those beliefs bring according to the opening description?
questions.answer: They solve the deep mystery of creation and bring happiness to the human spirit.

questions.question: What response to hardship is recommended before the comparison begins?
questions.answer: Turning to Allah with trust, patience, supplication, and thankfulness.

questions.question: Which religious duties are described as especially valuable for the life after death?
questions.answer: Listening to the Qur’an, obeying it, performing the prescribed prayers, and abandoning major sins.

questions.question: What kind of event does the passage invite the reader to listen to after the introduction?
questions.answer: A symbolic story used to explain spiritual truth.

questions.question: What physical condition is the soldier in at the start of the story?
questions.answer: He is badly wounded on both sides.

questions.question: What two external threats make his situation even more frightening?
questions.answer: A lion behind him and a gallows in front of him.

questions.question: What additional burden besides danger and pain does the soldier have to face?
questions.answer: He must also go on a long journey into exile.

questions.question: What feeling dominates the soldier before help comes?
questions.answer: Despair.

questions.question: How is the helper described in a way that suggests guidance from Allah?
questions.answer: He is presented as a compassionate, shining figure like Khidr.

questions.question: What are the first two items the helper gives, and what do they change?
questions.answer: Two talismans that turn the lion into a tame mount and the gallows into a pleasant swing.

questions.question: What are the next two items, and what do they do?
questions.answer: Two medicines that change the infected wounds into fragrant flowers.

questions.question: What final item is given, and what problem does it solve?
questions.answer: A ticket that makes the long journey quick and easy.

questions.question: How do both the soldier and Said respond after testing what was given?
questions.answer: Both confirm from experience that it is true.
